questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question: Identify the correct equation.
questions.solution: (d) Na2SO4 + BaCl2 → BaSO4↓ + 2NaCl is a correct, balanced precipitation reaction. (a) does not occur (insoluble base + salt); (b) is unbalanced (should give 2NaCl); (c) is balanced but the insoluble CaSO4 coats CaO and stops the reaction, so it is not used. Note: (c) is formally balanced; the expected key is (d).

questions.question:
Twinkle performed 3 experiments on compound X. And she observed the following:
i. Compound X turns blue litmus red.
ii. Dilute solution of compound X liberates a gas with rotten egg smell, when it is treated with sodium sulphide.
iii. Concentrated solution of compound X turns sugar crystals into a black spongy mass.
Compound X is:
questions.solution: (a) Sulphuric acid. It is acidic, liberates H2S from Na2S, and conc. H2SO4 dehydrates sugar to a black spongy mass of carbon.

questions.question: Ammonia is used in:
questions.solution: (b) Ostwald's process – ammonia is catalytically oxidised to make nitric acid (it is produced, not used, in Haber's process).

questions.question: The number of g atoms in 24 gm sulphur is: [At. Mass of S = 32]
An element X has 4 electrons in its outermost M shell. What will be its position in the periodic table?
questions.solution: (c) Period 3 group 14. Configuration 2,8,4 (silicon): three shells → period 3; 4 valence electrons → group 14.

questions.question: Two organic compounds A and B react with each other in presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to give a compound that has a fruity smell. The compounds A and B are:
questions.solution: (b) CH3OH and CH3COOH: an alcohol and a carboxylic acid form a fruity-smelling ester (methyl ethanoate).

questions.question: The common name of the compound with the molecular formula C2H4 is:
questions.solution: (a) Ethylene (ethene is the IUPAC name).

questions.question:
3 metal strips P, Q and R were put in 3 different beakers containing copper sulphate solution (Solutions A, B and C respectively). After some time, it was observed that:
i. Solution A was blue in colour.
ii. Solution B turned green.
iii. Solution C turned colourless.
Identify the metals P, Q and R:

options.a: P - Ag, Q - Mg, R - Fe
options.b: P - Mg, Q - Fe, R - Ag
options.c: P - Ag, Q - Fe, R - Mg
options.d: P - Fe, Q - Mg, R - Ag

questions.solution: (c) P – Ag (no displacement, stays blue), Q – Fe (FeSO4 is green), R – Mg (MgSO4 is colourless).

questions.question:
Assertion: Ammonia does not conduct electricity in gaseous or liquefied state.
Reason: Ions in gaseous ammonia or liquefied ammonia are not free to move.

options.a: Assertion and reason both are true, and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
options.b: Assertion and reason both are true and reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
options.c: Assertion is true but reason is false.
options.d: Assertion is false but reason is true.

questions.solution: (c) Assertion is true but reason is false. Ammonia is a covalent compound; gaseous or liquid NH3 contains molecules and no ions at all (not ions that are unable to move).

questions.topic: Yellow colour of lab nitric acid
questions.question:
Assertion: Nitric acid prepared in the laboratory is yellow in colour.
Reason: A reddish brown gas is used in its preparation.

options.a: Assertion and reason both are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of assertion,
options.b: Assertion and reason both are true, and Reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
options.c: Assertion is true but reason is false.
options.d: Assertion is false but reason is true.

questions.solution: (c) Assertion is true but reason is false. Lab HNO3 is yellow because some of it decomposes to NO2 which dissolves in it; it is prepared from KNO3 and conc. H2SO4, not from a reddish-brown gas.

questions.question: The number of bond pairs and lone pairs in chloroethane is:
questions.solution: (d) 7 & 3. C2H5Cl has 5 C–H, 1 C–C and 1 C–Cl bonds = 7 bond pairs; chlorine carries 3 lone pairs.

questions.question:
Which of the following is not true for dilute hydrochloric acid?
P. It is a volatile acid.
Q. It is an oxidising agent.
R. It is a monobasic acid.
S. It liberates a colourless odourless gas when zinc granules are added to it.
questions.solution: (d) Only Q. Dilute HCl is volatile, monobasic and liberates H2 with zinc, but it is not an oxidising agent.

questions.question: Which of the following contains the least number of moles?
questions.solution: (a) 11 g CO2 = 11/44 = 0.25 mol. Others: O2 = 1 mol; SO2 = 0.5 mol; Cl2 = 0.5 mol.

questions.question:
The set up below shows the electroplating of a steel spoon with silver. (Electrode X is a plate connected to the positive terminal of the battery; electrode Y is the spoon connected to the negative terminal.)
(a) Specify and identify the electrodes X and Y.
(b) Name the electrolyte used and give its molecular formula.
(c) Identify the spectator ions and give the anode reaction.
(d) Give balanced chemical equations for:
1. Thermal decomposition of silver nitrate.
2. Precipitation reaction with silver nitrate solution.
questions.solution:
(a) X – anode: block/plate of pure silver; Y – cathode: the steel spoon.
(b) Sodium argentocyanide, Na[Ag(CN)2].
(c) Spectator ions: Na⁺ and CN⁻ (also H⁺, OH⁻ from water) – they are not discharged. Anode: Ag − e⁻ → Ag⁺.
(d) 1. 2AgNO3 → 2Ag + 2NO2 + O2 (heat)
2. AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO3

marking_points.point: X anode pure silver, Y cathode steel spoon
Spectator ions Na+, CN- and anode Ag - e- → Ag+

questions.figure_desc: Electroplating cell: plate X connected to + terminal and spoon Y connected to − terminal dipped in electrolyte.

questions.question:
Match Column A with Column B.
Column A: (a) Carbon tetrachloride (b) Calcium oxide (c) Nickel at 300°C (d) Hydrogen chloride (e) Conc. sulphuric acid at 170°C
Column B: 1. Reduction of alkene 2. Non polar covalent compound 3. Ionic compound 4. Dehydration of alcohol 5. Polar covalent compound.
questions.solution:
(a) Carbon tetrachloride – 2. Non polar covalent compound
(b) Calcium oxide – 3. Ionic compound
(c) Nickel at 300°C – 1. Reduction of alkene (hydrogenation)
(d) Hydrogen chloride – 5. Polar covalent compound
(e) Conc. sulphuric acid at 170°C – 4. Dehydration of alcohol

questions.question:
Fill in the blanks: (Do not copy the statements)
(a) Metals have a tendency to ______ electrons and behave as ______ agents.
(b) Copper chloride solution gives ______ when it is treated with few drops of ammonium hydroxide, and ______ with excess ammonium hydroxide.
(c) The radius of a cation is ______ than its parent atom, whereas the radius of an anion is ______ than its parent atom.
(d) ______ is converted to zinc oxide by calcination, and ______ is converted to zinc oxide by roasting.
(e) The molecular formula of an alkane with 12 carbon atoms would be ______ and the molecular formula of an alcohol with 10 carbon atoms would be ______.
questions.solution:
(a) lose; reducing
(b) a pale blue precipitate (of Cu(OH)2); a deep/inky blue solution
(c) smaller; larger
(d) Zinc carbonate (calamine, ZnCO3); zinc sulphide (zinc blende, ZnS)
(e) C12H26; C10H21OH

questions.question: An organic compound X contains 48.64% carbon, 8.13% hydrogen and 43.23% oxygen. If the RMM of the compound is 74, find its molecular formula. [C = 12, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.solution:
C: 48.64/12 = 4.053; H: 8.13/1 = 8.13; O: 43.23/16 = 2.702.
Divide by 2.702: C 1.5, H 3.0, O 1 → multiply by 2: C 3, H 6, O 2.
Empirical formula C3H6O2; EF mass = 36 + 6 + 32 = 74.
n = 74/74 = 1, so molecular formula = C3H6O2.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give scientific reasons for the following:
(a) Sodalime is preferred to NaOH in the laboratory preparation of methane.
(b) The atomic size of fluorine is smaller than that of lithium.
(c) Hydrogen chloride gas is dissolved in water using an inverted funnel arrangement.
questions.solution:
(a) NaOH is deliquescent and attacks glass; soda lime (NaOH + CaO) is not deliquescent, keeps the mixture porous and dry, and CaO does not take part in the reaction.
(b) F and Li are in the same period; F has a higher nuclear charge (9 vs 3) with the same number of shells, so its electrons are pulled closer to the nucleus.
(c) HCl is highly soluble in water; the inverted funnel prevents back suction of water into the generating flask and gives a large surface area for absorption.

marking_points.point: Soda lime not deliquescent / CaO keeps it dry, NaOH attacks glass
Greater nuclear charge in same period pulls electrons closer
Prevents back suction; increases surface area

questions.question:
Identify the compounds E and F based on the following experimental observations:
(a) Compound E when heated with an alkali liberates a pungent smelling gas that turns Nessler's reagent brown. Aqueous solution of compound E when treated with barium chloride solution gives a white precipitate which is insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid.
(b) Compound F is an acid salt. It liberates a colourless, odourless gas that turns lime water milky when treated with dilute hydrochloric acid. An aqueous solution of compound F gives a white ppt. with excess sodium hydroxide solution.
questions.solution:
(a) E = ammonium sulphate, (NH4)2SO4 (NH3 with alkali; white BaSO4 insoluble in HCl).
(b) F = calcium hydrogen carbonate, Ca(HCO3)2 (acid salt; CO2 with HCl; Ca2+ gives white Ca(OH)2 precipitate insoluble in excess NaOH).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
The following questions relate to the electrolytic reduction of pure alumina:
(a) Why was electrolytic reduction chosen as the method for reducing alumina?
(b) Why is powdered coke sprinkled over the electrolytic mixture?
(c) Give the composition of the electrolytic mixture and justify the use of any one of its components.
(d) Give the electrode reactions.
questions.solution:
(a) Aluminium is highly reactive (high in the reactivity series) and has great affinity for oxygen, so Al2O3 cannot be reduced by common reducing agents like carbon; electrolysis is used.
(b) Coke reduces heat loss by radiation and prevents oxidation (burning) of the anode in air.
(c) Pure alumina (Al2O3) + cryolite (Na3AlF6) + fluorspar (CaF2). Cryolite lowers the fusion temperature from about 2050°C to 950°C and increases conductivity (fluorspar acts as solvent and lowers fusion temperature further).
(d) Cathode: 4Al3+ + 12e⁻ → 4Al; Anode: 6O2- − 12e⁻ → 3O2 (O2 then oxidises carbon anode: C + O2 → CO2).

marking_points.point: Al highly reactive, oxide not reduced by carbon
Coke reduces heat loss / prevents anode oxidation
Composition Al2O3 + cryolite + fluorspar with one justification
Cathode Al3+ + 3e- → Al and anode O2- - 2e- → O / 2O → O2

concepts: Zn(OH)2 and Pb(OH)2 both soluble in excess NaOH
only Zn(OH)2 soluble in excess NH4OH
questions.question:
Sanjana and Saima were both asked to distinguish Zinc nitrate and lead nitrate solutions in the laboratory. Sanjana added sodium hydroxide solution to both the solutions, whereas Saima added ammonium hydroxide to both the solutions.
(a) Who do you think will be successful in the task given? Justify your answer.
(b) Give another method by which you would have distinguished the two solutions.
questions.solution:
(a) Saima. With NaOH both give white precipitates (Zn(OH)2 and Pb(OH)2) which both dissolve in excess NaOH (both amphoteric), so Sanjana cannot tell them apart. With NH4OH both give white precipitates, but Zn(OH)2 dissolves in excess NH4OH (colourless solution) while Pb(OH)2 (chalky white) does not.
(b) Add dilute HCl (or dilute H2SO4): lead nitrate gives a white precipitate of PbCl2 (or PbSO4); zinc nitrate gives no precipitate.

marking_points.point: Justification: Zn(OH)2 soluble in excess NH4OH, Pb(OH)2 not; both soluble in excess NaOH
Another method: dil. HCl/H2SO4 gives white ppt only with lead nitrate

(b) Give the electron dot diagram for the formation of the compound formed between X and Y.

questions.question:
Give one observation for the following reactions and identify the property exhibited by the underlined compound.
(a) Ammonia (underlined) is treated with excess chlorine.
(b) Sulphur is treated with concentrated sulphuric acid (underlined).
questions.solution:
(a) NH3 + 3Cl2 → NCl3 + 3HCl. Observation: the greenish-yellow chlorine forms a yellow, oily, explosive liquid (nitrogen trichloride). Property: ammonia acts as a reducing agent.
(b) S + 2H2SO4 → 3SO2 + 2H2O. Observation: a colourless, pungent gas (SO2) is evolved which turns acidified K2Cr2O7 green. Property: conc. H2SO4 acts as an oxidising agent.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
(a) 12 litres of hydrogen combines with 8 litres of nitrogen to prepare ammonia. Calculate the volume of ammonia produced. The ammonia formed is passed through an inverted funnel arrangement. Calculate the volume of residual gases if any.
(b) Give the statement of the law on which the above numerical is based.
questions.solution:
(a) N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3 (1 : 3 : 2 by volume). 12 L H2 reacts with 4 L N2 to give 8 L NH3. Unreacted N2 = 8 − 4 = 4 L. Ammonia (8 L) dissolves in water in the inverted funnel arrangement, so residual gas = 4 L of nitrogen.
(b) Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes: when gases react, they do so in volumes which bear a simple whole-number ratio to one another and to the volumes of the gaseous products, all measured at the same temperature and pressure.

(c) Calculate the percentage composition of oxygen in blue vitriol. (H = 1, O = 16, S = 32, Cu = 64)
questions.solution:

(c) Blue vitriol CuSO4·5H2O: M = 64 + 32 + 64 + 90 = 250. Oxygen = 4 + 5 = 9 atoms = 144 g. % O = 144/250 × 100 = 57.6%.
